judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short instructional note that ownership passes to the deceased Owner's estate unless a contingent owner is named; the concept is definite even though the OCR mangles it, and no term carries two reasonable meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the Owner/Contingent Owner designation blanks on the same application page and nothing in the policy or Statement of Policy Cost contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional instruction about listing an excluded spouse in 'Special Requests'; the underlying direction is administrative and the only obscurity is transcription noise rather than a genuine choice of meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It corresponds to the Family Plan / Term Rider checkboxes in the Plan of Insurance section and to the 'Special Requests' box, with no competing provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is the representation that the insured read the completed application and that a false statement or material misrepresentation 'may result in loss of coverage' — 'material misrepresentation' and the permissive 'may' are exactly the words a rescission fight turns on, and the text as rendered says 'only false statement' where 'any' was plainly meant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the truth-and-completeness clause (c004), which qualifies answers by 'to the best of my knowledge and belief', creating tension between an absolute falsity trigger and a subjective knowledge standard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'True and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief' is a classic contestable standard — subjective good faith versus objective accuracy — and 'the basis of any policy issued' invites argument about incorporation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against c003's misrepresentation warning and against condition (3) in c008 that the answers 'remain true and complete, without material change', so the three clauses state the same duty in different terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An acknowledgement of receipt of the Limited Temporary Insurance Agreement and acceptance of its terms; the operative content is a receipt, with no named ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates a Temporary Insurance Agreement that is not reproduced in this instrument and is carved out of the no-coverage-until-delivery clause (c006), which leaves the interim coverage terms outside the document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'no policy shall be in force unless and until' language is a condition precedent to coverage, but the clause as rendered is cut off mid-sentence so its conditions cannot be read from the provision itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly excepts the Temporary Insurance Agreement acknowledged in c005 and is completed by c008's numbered conditions, so its meaning depends entirely on documents and text elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory fraud warning; it is boilerplate notice rather than an operative promise and creates no real interpretive choice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is duplicated in substance at c011 and c019 with no inconsistency in the obligations they describe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The numbered conditions — delivery, payment of the full first premium during the lifetime of all persons to be insured, and answers remaining true and complete 'without material change' as of the date of delivery — turn on 'material change', a boundary term parties genuinely dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It completes c006 and overlaps c004's knowledge-qualified representation, so whether the applicant warrants continuing accuracy absolutely or only to her belief is unresolved across the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Acceptance of the policy is deemed acceptance of corrections noted in the Home Office Endorsements, with a carve-out apparently requiring written agreement for certain changes; the interaction of deemed consent and required written consent is left blurred in the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties to the 'Home Office Endorsements' box on the application, which is blank here, so the deemed-acceptance mechanism has nothing in the instrument to operate on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The agent-authority limitation ('no agent is authorized to make or change a contract ... nor waive any of Ohio National's rights') is standard, but the negative list is illustrative and its reach over an agent's completion of answers is left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stands against the agent's certification at c012 that the agent recorded the applicant's answers, the recurring point of tension when an application is later challenged as inaccurate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A second rendering of the criminal fraud notice; purely declaratory of statutory penalties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cumulative with c007 and c019 and consistent with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The agent certifies the information was 'truly and accurately recorded' as supplied by the applicant; 'as supplied by the applicant' allocates responsibility but the clause does not say what follows if it was not.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against c010's disclaimer of agent authority and against c003/c004's placing of responsibility for the answers on the insured.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad HIPAA-style authorization to a long list of addressees for 'any and all information, records or knowledge'; the enumerated list closed by 'and/or employer' is broad but the grant itself is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is repeated nearly verbatim at c021/c025 on the medical exam form, with the same scope and no contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Good, as needed, for 24 months from the date signed or while I have a claim, if longer' — the open-ended extension 'while I have a claim' is imprecise, but the 24-month rule is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates c023 on the medical exam form in identical terms, so there is no cross-document inconsistency to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line photocopy-equals-original clause; simple and self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrored at c024 with the same effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgement of receipt of the Notice of Information Practices; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Notice itself is not in the instrument, but no other provision depends on its content.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scope clause sweeps medical history plus 'financial, employment or personal information' with no stated limit other than insurance purposes; 'personal information' is broad but the catch-all is expressly cabined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the parallel grant at c025 and with the release limits at c018.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Release is allowed to reinsurers, MIB and 'others who perform business or legal services related to my application or the policy', then barred to 'anyone else' unless required or permitted by law — 'permitted by law' is a wide exception that swallows much of the prohibition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is duplicated at c022 in identical terms; no other provision restricts disclosure differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Part 2 fraud warning, again a statutory recitation of criminal exposure rather than an operative contract term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c007 and c011.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is a truncated fragment — 'A copy of this application will' — so as it stands it states no complete proposition, though the intended sense (attached to and part of the policy) is a standard incorporation term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats the incorporation sentence in c004 for the Part 2 application; whether both Parts 1 and 2 form the basis of the policy is the sort of scope point that matters in a rescission dispute.
